form.label: Remediation
form.description: What has actually been fixed, and what merely stopped being reported.

search.query: | `riskability_open_findings` | search hostname=$host_tok|s$ | stats dc(finding_key) AS n
| `riskability_findings_now` | search hostname=$host_tok|s$ | where status="mitigated" | stats dc(finding_key) AS n

single.option: package upgraded at the same path

search.query: | `riskability_findings_now` | search hostname=$host_tok|s$ | where status="removed" | stats dc(finding_key) AS n

single.option: package no longer at that path

search.query: | `riskability_findings_now` | search hostname=$host_tok|s$ | where status="unknown" | stats dc(finding_key) AS n

panel.title: How long findings stay open, by severity

search.query: | inputlookup riskability_openstate_dim_lookup | where dim="severity" | rename value AS sev, age_lo AS lo, age_q1 AS q1, age_med AS med, age_q3 AS q3, age_hi AS hi | where cves >= 3 | sort 50000 - cves | fields sev, lo, q1, med, q3, hi

viz.option: Not enough open findings to describe an age distribution.

div.b: Age is time since Riskability first saw the finding.
div.span: Not since the CVE was published, and not since the host became vulnerable. On a recent install every box is short; the number means something only once collection has run longer than your patch cycle.
Click a box above to narrow the two tables below.

panel.title: Mitigated: the upgrade that fixed it - $rem_sev_label$

search.query: | `riskability_mitigated_findings` | search hostname=$host_tok|s$ | eval sev = coalesce(severity, "unrated") | search $rem_sev_filter$ | eval fixed_after_days = round((last_seen - first_seen)/86400, 1) | eval root = if(scope_id!="", scope_id, "host") | table cve_id, package, ecosystem, mitigation, root, hostname, path, fixed_after_days, epss | rename cve_id AS "CVE", package AS "Package", ecosystem AS "Type", mitigation AS "Version change", root AS "Root", hostname AS "Host", path AS "Path", fixed_after_days AS "Open for (days)", epss AS "EPSS" | sort 50000 - "EPSS"

viz.option: Nothing observed being fixed yet. Mitigation is visible only once a host reports the same path at a newer version.

panel.title: Closed without evidence of a fix

html.p: These stopped being reported, but either the package is no longer at that path or the host stopped reporting entirely. Neither is proof of remediation: a failed scan, a decommissioned host, and a feed imported without the relevant ecosystem all look like this. Hence the separate table.

search.query: | `riskability_findings_now` | search hostname=$host_tok|s$ | eval sev = coalesce(severity, "unrated") | search $rem_sev_filter$ | where status="removed" OR status="unknown" | eval root = if(scope_id!="", scope_id, "host") | table cve_id, package, last_version, status, root, hostname, path, last_seen | eval last_seen = strftime(last_seen, "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M") | rename cve_id AS "CVE", package AS "Package", last_version AS "Last seen version", status AS "Status", root AS "Root", hostname AS "Host", path AS "Path", last_seen AS "Last reported"

viz.option: Nothing here, the good case: every finding that stopped appearing did so with evidence of an upgrade.

panel.title: Findings first seen, the last 90 days

search.query: | `riskability_findings_now` | search hostname=$host_tok|s$ | where first_seen >= relative_time(now(), "-90d") | eval day = strftime(first_seen, "%Y-%m-%d") | stats dc(finding_key) AS findings BY day, status | sort 50000 day

viz.option: No findings recorded yet. This chart fills in as scans accumulate.

div.b: This is when Riskability first saw a finding, not when it appeared.
div.span: Bars cluster around scan and feed-import times rather than real events, so the shape reflects the collection schedule as much as the fleet. Read whether the open band is shrinking; a quiet day is not a good day.
